SketchyUp's vendored SketchUp (.skp) reader: source record (ADR 0176, R102.d)
==========================================================================

This file is installed as share/doc/sketchyup/SKP-SOURCE.txt. It says where the code in
sketchyup-skp-worker came from, which licence it carries and how the vendored copy is checked.

Reader: OpenSKP, the parser subset only
  Upstream:   https://github.com/iamahsanmehmood/openskp
  Commit:     23a15e8742e936694bf14aa029cb0e2862dce5b9 (2026-10-22)
  Archive:    https://github.com/iamahsanmehmood/openskp/archive/23a15e8742e936694bf14aa029cb0e2862dce5b9.tar.gz
  SHA-256:    5b304cc024b2d72504ac5a6676968166fdd300f180d3f1078efe8b959951e1a5
  Licence:    MIT (LICENSE in this directory; installed as OpenSKP-LICENSE)
  Copyright:  Copyright (c) 2024-2026 Ahsan Mehmood

miniz: the ZIP container reader that OpenSKP's VFF container uses
  Upstream:   https://github.com/richgel999/miniz
  Commit:     77d0dce8627735138c51770d1799a1ef48f2117d (2026-07-01)
  Archive:    https://github.com/richgel999/miniz/archive/77d0dce8627735138c51770d1799a1ef48f2117d.tar.gz
  SHA-256:    baa14349e7c5efb4a493a03af7d2f29d0ef45d87d488567fe5360edb33f8b7ba
  Licence:    MIT (miniz/LICENSE; installed as miniz-LICENSE)

Both are MIT, the same licence as SketchyUp, and their notices ship with the package
(THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES).

What is vendored
  The model, the VFF (2021 and later) and MFC CArchive (2013 to 2020, and older) containers,
  the TLV and page/dimension decoding, the attribute and transform support, the public
  headers and the miniz files the build uses. Excluded: the exporters, the writer, the scene
  baker, tinygltf and flatbuffers. The exact file list is the SUBSET table in
  scripts/vendor-openskp.py, and VENDOR.txt gives the SHA-256 of every vendored file.

Changes to the upstream files (MIT permits them; all six are recorded in PATCHES.md)
  - src/parser.cpp: the four scene-builder wrappers that call the excluded scene baker are
    removed.
  - src/internal.hpp: the umbrella include is replaced by the public headers the sources use, and
    RawDefinition gains the definition's attribute dictionaries.
  - include/openskp/model.hpp: Definition gains attribute_dictionaries (the definition's own
    dictionaries, as Instance has).
  - src/model.cpp: definition() copies the raw dictionaries into Definition.
  - src/geometry.cpp: collect_definitions reads a VFF definition's dictionaries from its entity base.
  - src/legacy.cpp: the CComponentDefinition reader keeps its attribute container, and the definition
    loop reads it.

Not affiliated with Trimble
  OpenSKP is an independent, open-source implementation built by reverse engineering the
  file format. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Trimble Inc. SketchUp is a trademark
  of Trimble Inc. SketchyUp is not affiliated with or endorsed by Trimble Inc.

Where the code runs
  Only sketchyup-skp-worker links the parser. The application and sketchyup-cli do not
  (scripts/verify-skp-library.py checks this on every installed build).

How the vendored copy is checked
  scripts/vendor-openskp.py fetch DIR     downloads the two pinned archives and checks them
  scripts/vendor-openskp.py check DIR     fails unless every vendored file equals the pinned
                                          upstream file (with the patches applied)
  scripts/vendor-openskp.py pin           checks that VENDOR.txt, PATCHES.md and
                                          dependencies.json record these pins
  The CI "SKP parser, helper and import" job runs the first two on every run it selects.

Fixtures
  The .skp files under tests/fixtures/skp/ are written by OpenSKP's own writer at the pinned
  commit, not made in SketchUp. Their provenance and SHA-256 values are in
  tests/fixtures/skp/SKP-SOURCE.txt.

Pin
  The pin is not moved by this record. A move is a reviewed change: re-run
  vendor-openskp.py update from the new archives, prove that the subset compiles and that
  parse_skp links, and re-run the corpus (ADR 0176, implementation notes R102.d).
